Section 3  Nutrition in the Clinical Setting
Polyunsaturated Fats
The two major categories of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) are omega-6 
and omega-3 fatty acids. Vegetable oils such as corn, canola, cottonseed, peanut, 
sunflower, safflower, and soybean contain omega-6 fatty acids.19 Linoleic acid, an 
essential omega-6 fatty acid, cannot be synthesized by the body and is therefore 
required in the diet.13 Arachidonic acid, which is synthesized from linoleic acid, is 
the major omega-6 fatty acid found in cell membranes and the precursor of prosta-
glandins. Substitution of PUFA for saturated fat in the diet lowers LDL-C and 
reduces risk for CHD.21
